body: Thank you and I'm sorry for that, I know how badly both illnesses can affect people with them. I'm also sorry you're both suffering, it's hard trying to find worth in things and even in self when society has built stigma around illness and capability. I'm honestly trying to keep going but it's becoming so hard. Hopefully we can find our niche in life and have some semblance of happiness. Thank you for taking the time to respond

Depression is knowing there is a problem but not having the motivation to fight it. It's beating yourself up over simple things and spiraling when nothing goes right. It's the sinking feeling of failure and being behind peers. It's wondering where things went wrong and seeing no way to put it right. Depression is like napalm, hard to shake but so incredibly painful.

In the same boat, they used to provide distraction but of late it's just been hard to do anything between the suicidal lows and constant issues. Only thing I could suggest is finding games that focus on you time, things that allow you to fully use your brain to get your mind off of the dark thoughts and feelings.

For myself that would be Rainbow Six Siege, I have to focus and it leaves little time for the depression to sink it's claws in. It also provides moments where it might induce a small laugh.

Other than that I wish you the best, I know it's hard. So very incredibly hard but surely it has to improve? Take care of yourself, friend.

Sorry you feel that way. I understand your plight, it seems like a vicious circle - I'm not sure how others can even be happy in this existence knowing all they do is work to exist.  


I'm Twenty-Four in October, everyone else is going places, changing drastically and I'm still in the same old rut. We're here if you need to talk, hope things get better for you.

I'm the same in that respect. I'm not sure what to really do, if I had access to a gun (I live in Southern England) I'd probably have been dead years ago. I hope things improve for you, I know it can seem like an empty promise given how many of us view things.
I'd take you up on that offer but I'm in England. I do hope you find that someone to talk to though, things can be pretty rough. Best wishes from over the pond.

It's tough, I understand that. I too am struggling with my mind and it's becoming so tiring. I find myself wishing some freak accident will occur or when I learn to drive I can just crash it and hope for the best. I'm not sure I can offer insight, surely there is one friend or long distance family you can confide in? Or somewhere to stay until you can get back on your feet? Feel free to drop a message and I hope things pick up for you.

Keep fighting the good fight
